proposedTopics.title: Debugging: traces & the interactive debugger
proposedTopics.description: `-vvv` prints execution traces for failing tests; `-vvvv` prints them for all tests and adds setup traces for failures. The decoded call frames, returns, reverts, and logs turn a failure into a navigable execution path. For opcode-level inspection, `forge test --debug --match-test <regex>` launches Foundry's interactive TUI debugger for one matching function, showing opcodes, source, stack, and memory while `j`/`k`, `c`/`C`, `s`, and `g`/`G` navigate the transaction.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: intentionally break a test in test/phase03/ (e.g. a wrong assert value), run `forge test -vvv --match-test <regex>` on it, and paste the relevant trace frames into contracts/phase03/debugging-notes.md explaining which call reverted; then run `forge test --debug --match-test <regex>` on the same test and record one documented navigation command used to reach the relevant opcode. Done when: debugging-notes.md documents both diagnoses, then the fixed test passes.

proposedTopics.title: Gas snapshots
proposedTopics.description: `forge snapshot` records gas used by each test in `.gas-snapshot`; `forge snapshot --check` compares a fresh run with that baseline and fails when an entry changes. Committing the snapshot turns gas changes—both increases and decreases—into an explicit review decision instead of an unnoticed side effect.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: run `forge snapshot` after writing a function in contracts/phase03/, then deliberately change its gas and run `forge snapshot --check`. Done when: the check fails on the changed entry and passes again after restoring the code or intentionally regenerating the reviewed baseline.

proposedTopics.title: Scripting & deployment (forge script)
proposedTopics.description: A Foundry script is a Solidity contract with a `run()` entry point. Calls at the broadcast depth between `vm.startBroadcast()` and `vm.stopBroadcast()` are collected as transactions; Forge simulates them first and sends them only when `--broadcast` is present. Supplying an RPC URL makes the dry run use that chain state, while a local Anvil URL keeps both runs local.

proposedTopics.title: Contract verification
proposedTopics.description: `forge verify-contract` submits an address, contract identifier, compiler inputs, and ABI-encoded constructor arguments to a selected verifier. Sourcify calls byte-for-byte agreement including compiler metadata an exact match; agreement after excluding metadata is a match (formerly partial match). Verifiers differ, so the command must name the provider and reproduce the deployment settings.

Done when: the notes use `cast abi-encode` correctly, reproduce compiler settings, name the verifier, and use Sourcify's current match terminology.

proposedTopics.title: Dependency management: git submodules
proposedTopics.description: By default, `forge install <org/repo>@<tag-or-rev>` adds source under `lib/` as a Git submodule. The superproject records the submodule URL in `.gitmodules` and its checked-out commit as a gitlink; Foundry also maintains `foundry.lock` for requested tags or revisions. A clone must initialize submodules before imports can resolve.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: run `forge install OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts@<reviewed-tag>` in web3-practice and record the resulting `lib/` entry, `.gitmodules` entry, gitlink commit, and `foundry.lock` record in contracts/phase03/deps.md. Done when: `forge build` resolves an import and deps.md explains why `git submodule update --init --recursive` is needed after a fresh clone.

proposedTopics.title: remappings.txt & import resolution
proposedTopics.description: A remapping rewrites a Solidity import prefix to a filesystem path—for example, `@openzeppelin/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/`. Foundry reads explicit entries from `foundry.toml` or `remappings.txt` and, by default, auto-detects additional mappings by scanning library directories; `forge remappings` prints the resolved table.

proposedTopics.title: soldeer package manager
proposedTopics.description: Soldeer is Foundry's registry-based package manager: `forge soldeer install <name>~<version-requirement>` resolves a package into `dependencies/`, records it under `[dependencies]`, and locks the selected release in `soldeer.lock`. It can share a project with other managers, but duplicate packages and colliding remappings must be avoided.

Done when: `forge build` resolves a version-qualified import from the Soldeer package and deps.md notes the duplicate-dependency/remapping caveat.

proposedTopics.title: foundry.toml profiles
proposedTopics.description: `foundry.toml` supports named `[profile.<name>]` tables, with `default` selected unless `FOUNDRY_PROFILE` names another. A CI profile can override `fuzz.runs` while the local default stays fast; `forge config` under each environment shows the effective values before tests run.

proposedTopics.title: Static analysis: Slither & Aderyn wiring
proposedTopics.description: Slither and Aderyn statically analyze Solidity without needing a test to execute the vulnerable path. Their detector sets can flag patterns such as uninitialized state or unchecked calls, but findings require triage: a report is evidence to investigate, not proof that every warning is exploitable.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What do `-vvv` and `-vvvv` add to `forge test` output, and when would you choose each?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: `-vvv` prints execution traces for failing tests. `-vvvv` prints traces for all tests and setup traces for failures. Start with `-vvv` to isolate a failure; use `-vvvv` when a passing path or setup needs comparison. Pitfall: broad trace output becomes noisy on fuzz or invariant campaigns, so combine it with a test filter.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How do you launch Foundry's interactive debugger for one specific test, and what do `C`, `s`, and `G` navigate to?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Run `forge test --debug --match-test "<regex>"` with a pattern that selects one function. `C` moves to the next call-type instruction, `s` to the next `JUMPDEST`, and `G` to the end of the transaction. Pitfall: `s` is not a source-level step-into command, and the current debugger has no documented `o` step-out binding.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does `forge snapshot --check` actually fail the build on, and what must you do after an intentional gas increase?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It diffs the current run's gas-per-test against the committed .gas-snapshot file and fails if it changed. Pitfall: an intentional increase (e.g. added a safety check) needs .gas-snapshot regenerated and committed, or every future CI run fails on that line forever.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What can branch/line coverage from forge coverage reveal that 'all tests pass' doesn't?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: An untested revert branch, an unreached else, or a function only ever exercised on one code path. Pitfall: 100% line coverage doesn't mean every input combination or invariant is tested — coverage measures reached code, not correctness.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What's the difference between running a forge script with and without --broadcast?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Without `--broadcast`, Forge collects and simulates the marked transactions but sends nothing. With it, calls and creations at the broadcast call depth between `vm.startBroadcast()` and `vm.stopBroadcast()` are signed and sent after simulation succeeds. Pitfall: a dry run uses remote state only when an RPC/fork URL is supplied; otherwise it is a local EVM simulation.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a minimal forge script deploying a Counter with a constructor arg of 42.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: function run() external { vm.startBroadcast(); new Counter(42); vm.stopBroadcast(); }

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why must compiler settings match exactly for forge verify-contract to succeed, even when the source is 'the same'?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: The verifier recompiles the submitted sources with the supplied compiler version, optimizer, EVM, and other settings, then compares the result with deployed bytecode. Sourcify calls byte-for-byte agreement including metadata an exact match and agreement excluding metadata a match. A setting that changes executable bytecode fails both. Pitfall: constructor arguments must be ABI-encoded exactly as deployed with `cast abi-encode`, and match labels vary by verifier.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What breaks if a fresh clone of a Foundry repo skips `git submodule update --init --recursive` before `forge build`?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: The superproject has gitlinks but the dependency working trees under `lib/` are absent, so imports fail; `--recursive` also initializes nested submodules. The recorded gitlink identifies a commit, while `foundry.lock` preserves requested tag/revision intent. Pitfall: an unqualified first install follows the repository's default ref at install time, so choose a reviewed tag or revision explicitly.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does a line like `@openzeppelin/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/` in remappings.txt do, and what does `forge remappings` show beyond what you wrote by hand?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It rewrites any import starting with @openzeppelin/ to resolve under lib/openzeppelin-contracts/. forge remappings prints the FULL resolved table, including entries auto-inferred from installed dependencies. Pitfall: a typo'd prefix fails silently as 'file not found', not as a remapping error.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a remappings.txt line mapping forge-std imports to lib/forge-std/src/.
How does installing a dependency with soldeer differ from forge install for a git submodule, in terms of where the dependency's version is recorded?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Soldeer records a version requirement under `[dependencies]`, resolves source under `dependencies/`, and records the exact resolution in `soldeer.lock`; default `forge install` uses a Git submodule under `lib/`, with `.gitmodules`, a gitlink commit, and `foundry.lock`. Pitfall: the managers can coexist, but do not install the same package twice or let their remappings collide.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does FOUNDRY_PROFILE change which foundry.toml settings apply, and why give [profile.ci] more fuzz runs than [profile.default]?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci makes Foundry read [profile.ci], falling back to [profile.default] for any key it doesn't override. Fewer runs locally means fast iteration; more runs in CI means a fuller check before merge, without changing test code. Pitfall: a key missing from [profile.ci] silently inherits from [profile.default] — an incomplete profile isn't an error, just a partial override.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a foundry.toml block giving the ci profile 1024 fuzz runs.
What class of bug can Slither/Aderyn catch that a passing test suite might miss, and why?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Static analyzers flag patterns like reentrancy-prone external calls before state updates, unchecked low-level call returns, or uninitialized state — by reading code structure, not executing it, so they catch a bug class even if no test happens to exercise that exact path. Pitfall: static analysis produces false positives routinely — triage findings, don't blindly 'fix' every warning.
